task_title: Complete published context read contract for a Scripture scope
result: PASS — published-only bundle RPC, TypeScript contracts, runtime validation, Supabase repository and tests all pass.
user_visible_outcome: No screen change. A consumer can now fetch one complete, validated context bundle for a Scripture scope through the mobile repository boundary: passage contexts, localized entities, claims with source references, mentions with render spans, relevance, relationships and events (participants and places), all in deterministic order using stable keys. Drafts never appear.
files_changed: supabase/tests/10_published_context_bundle_test.sql (new: synthetic published fixture + draft denial + deterministic order)
apps/mobile/src/content/publishedContext.ts (new: Zod contract, runtime validation, deterministic-order checks, PublishedContextError)
apps/mobile/__tests__/published-content.test.ts (fake repos updated for the new method)

read_api.surface: public_content.published_context_bundle(p_scope_key text) returns jsonb. One call returns the whole bundle for a scope.
read_api.bundle_keys: scope_key, contexts[], entities[] (names + descriptions), claims[] (citations), mentions[] (start/end utf16 spans), relevance[], relationships[], events[] (participants, places).
read_api.stable_keys: entity_key/claim_key/scope_key and book_osis + chapter + verse + local_key + edition_key; no surrogate ids cross the boundary.
read_api.deterministic_order: contexts by kind; entities/claims/relevance/events by key; names by (language_tag, normalized_form, kind); descriptions by (locale, revision); citations by (locator, support_kind); mentions by (book, chapter, verse, entity_key, occurrence_ordinal); relationships by (subject, predicate, object).
read_api.security: Read-only, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER with pinned search_path. Every branch filters to published rows (published package membership and/or review_state='published'; mentions require edition.status='published'). Execute granted to anon/authenticated; no private table is exposed directly. Chosen over N invoker views because the bundle joins many private tables with per-table publication rules; gating happens once, centrally, and is covered by published-only and draft-denial tests.
read_api.why: Contexts, claims, mentions, relevance, relationships and events were not previously readable by clients; only entities/attestations/verses were. This adds the complete scope bundle the mobile boundary needs.

runtime_validation: apps/mobile/src/content/publishedContext.ts defines strict Zod schemas (unknown fields rejected), span and digest checks, and superRefine checks that every array is in the server's deterministic order. parsePublishedContextBundle throws PublishedContextError on any defect; the repository validates before returning, and the store maps failures to null.

tests.sql_10: Seeds a synthetic published scope (published entities/names/descriptions/claim+citation/context section/edition+mention+span/relevance/relationship/event+participant+place) plus a draft entity, draft description and draft claim; asserts anon receives the full bundle with correct keys, spans, ordering and counts, and that draft rows never appear.
tests.mobile: Contract: parses a complete ordered bundle; rejects missing sections, malformed digests, bad spans, unknown fields and non-deterministic order. Adapter: calls published_context_bundle with the scope key and validates the payload; throws on backend error or invalid payload. Store: returns the bundle through the boundary, and null (never throws) when unconfigured or failing.

known_limitations: The curated Nehemiah 2 draft is not published, so a live bundle is empty until a publication release exists; the contract is proven with synthetic published fixtures.

claim_citations.source_release_id is a deterministic local uuid (registry release rows are not created); the bundle exposes the source edition key and the citation locator/digest rather than a registry release key.
The bundle is remote-only by design: no SQLite caching was added (per instruction).
SECURITY DEFINER is a deliberate, documented trade-off for this public read API; it is read-only, pinned, and published-filtered, but it does bypass RLS internally.
stop_condition: Stopped after the complete context bundle can be fetched and validated through the mobile repository boundary, with published-only and draft-denial tests passing. No publication, no screens, no SQLite cache expansion, no other chapter, no unrelated table changes.
